Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

I welcome all of you to special functions, which is your fifth unit in engineering mathematics one.

Key details

  • In this unit, you are going to learn gamma function, beta function, and basis function.
  • In this particular class, we are going to discuss definition of gamma function.
  • Properties of gamma function and graph of gamma function.
  • Gamma function is a definite integral whose integrant depends on one variable.
  • It is also known as Euler's integral of second kind.
  • It is the generalization of factorial notation from integes to real numbers.
  • We can define gamma function as.
  • Gamma of n is equal to integral zero to infinity t power minus x power n minus one dx n greater than c.
  • Thus gamma n defines a function of n for positive values of n.
  • From this result we can obtain the value of gamma.
  • Then we get gamma 1 is equal to integral 0 to infinity e power minus x power 1 minus 1 dx.
  • x power 1 minus 1 is x power 0 and we know x power 0 is 1, so it just reduces to integral 0 to infinity e power minus x bx.
  • And we know that integration of e power minus x dx is equal to e power minus x divided by minus 1.
  • Using the fact that e power minus infinity is equal to 0 and e power 0 is equal to 1, we can evaluate this to 1.
  • Thus we have gamma of 1 is equal to 1.
  • We can have an alternate form of gamma function.
  • We can obtain it easily by using definition of gamma function.
  • We know that gamma n is equal to integral 0 to infinity t power minus x power n minus 1 dx.
  • If x is t square, dx is 2t d.
  • Therefore, gamma n is equal to integral 0 to infinity e power minus t square t square to the power n minus 1 2 t dt.
  • Observe here, after this substitution, the limits of integration do not change because when x is equal to 0, your t is also 0.
  • When x is infinity, t is also infinite.
  • This is another form of gamma function.
  • While solving problems on gamma function, we can make use of any of these two forms according to our convenience.
  • Next, we will discuss some properties of gamma function.
  • First of them is reduction formula.
  • It states that gamma of n plus 1 is equal to n gamma n where n is a real number.
  • We can prove this easily by using the definition of gamma function, which is.
  • Gamma n is equal to integral 0 to infinity e power minus x power n minus 1 dx.
  • We want gamma of n plus 1.
  • which is equal to integral 0 to infinity e power minus x power n dx.
  • We have to evaluate this integral by using integration by parts.

Example or application from the lecture

  • In this expression, let us substitute x is equal to t square.
  • We know already that integration by parts is given by integral uv dx is equal to u into integral v dx minus integral of derivative of u or d by dx of u into integral of v dx.

Core explanation · 05:00–09:59

When you take x power n is equal to u and e power minus x is equal to v, you will get it as x power n e power minus x divided by minus 1 plus n into integral 0 to infinity.

Key details

  • E power minus x power n minus one dx.
  • When you substitute the limits of integration for the first term,.
  • E power minus infinity zero and e power zero is one.
  • So first term becomes a zero and observe the second term along with n, you have integral zero to infinity, e power minus x, x power n minus one.
  • dx which is nothing but equal to gamma n.
  • When n is a negative non-integer, the formula used to find gamma of n is gamma n is equal to gamma of n plus 1 divided by n.
  • Remember, gamma n is not defined for n is equal to 0.
  • And it is also not defined when n is a negative integer.
  • But we can find the value of gamma n if n is negative real number which is not a negative integer using this formula.
  • When n is a positive integer, gamma of n plus one is equal to n factory.
  • We can prove this easily by using reduction formula which states gamma of n plus 1 is equal to n gamma n.
  • That is 1, because we know gamma 1 is equal to 1.
  • When we put n is equal to 2, we get gamma of 3, that is 2 gamma 2, which is 2 factorial.
  • When you put n is equal to 3, we get gamma 4, which is 3 gamma 3, that is 3 factorial.
  • And when you put n is equal to 4, we get gamma 5, which is 4 gamma 4, that is 4 factor.
  • Just look at the pattern here.
  • Gamma two is one factorial, gamma three is two factorial, gamma four is three factorial, and gamma five is four factorial.
  • Gamma of n plus 1 is equal to n factorial where n is a positive integer.
  • Remember, gamma n is not defined when n is 0 or when n is a negative integer.
  • Gamma half value we can find now.
  • Gamma half is equal to square root of pi.
  • We can prove this by considering alternate form of gamma function, which is gamma n is equal to 2 times integral 0 to infinity e power minus x square x to the power 2n minus 1 dx.
  • Which can also be written as two times integral 0 to infinity e power minus y square dy.
  • Because since we are dealing with definite integrals, here x is a dummy variable.
  • You can write it as x or y or t or any variable since we are dealing with definite integrals.
  • which is equal to four times integral 0 to infinity 0 to infinity e power minus x square plus y square dx d y.
  • Then x square plus y square is equal to r square.

Example or application from the lecture

  • Let us put n is equal to 1 in this formula, we get gamma 2 is equal to 1, gamma 1.
  • Let us put n is equal to half in this expression.

Key details

  • And observe the limits for x and y.
  • Both are varying from 0 to infinity.
  • That means both x and y are positive.
  • So our region of integration is the first quadrant.
  • In this first quadrant, r value varies from 0 to infinity and theta value varies from 0 to pi by 2.
  • Then it can be written as four into integral 0 to pi by 2 b theta into integral 0 to infinity e power minus r square r br.
  • When you integrate the first integral 0 to pi by 2 d theta, integration of d theta is theta, substitute the limits of integration, it reduces to 4 into pi by 2.
  • into integral 0 to infinity e power minus r square r dr.
  • That is equal to 2 by into minus 1 by 2 e power minus r square limits vary from 0 to infinity.
  • Thus, we get gamma half the whole square is equal to pi, so we can conclude gamma half is equal to square root of pi, which is a very important result.
  • This is the graph of gamma function.
  • Observe here, gamma function is continuous for positive values of n and it is not continuous for negative values of n.
  • We can find or you can plot this curve by using the properties gamma of n plus 1 is equal to n gamma n.
  • Gamma n is equal to gamma n plus 1 divided by n.
  • This is for negative real numbers which are not indigenous.
  • And gamma half is equal to square root of pi.
